meta.name: squish-golden-retrieval-v1
meta.description: Golden fixture corpus and query set for retrieval quality evaluation. All content describes a fictional research org (Helios Research Lab) so cases are self-contained and verifiable against corpus text.
meta.notes: mustHit = memories that directly answer the query (any of them at rank 1 counts as a hit@1; set membership drives Recall@5 and MRR). mayHit = supporting/related memories worth surfacing but not required. Expected IDs are derived from explicit statements in the corpus, not vibes.

memories.content: Decision: use PostgreSQL over MongoDB for experiment metadata because we need strong relational integrity across runs and datasets; JSONB columns cover the flexible fields where a document store would have helped.
Decision: standardize on pnpm for all TypeScript monorepos instead of npm or yarn; strict lockfiles and content-addressable storage cut install time and disk usage roughly in half.
Decision: build the annotation service on FastAPI rather than Flask because async endpoints handle concurrent labeling sessions better and pydantic gives us request validation for free.

Decision: use Redis Streams as the event relay between ingestion workers instead of Kafka; our peak throughput is under 5k messages per second and Kafka's operational overhead is not justified at this scale.
Decision: fine-tune Mistral-7B in-house for the ticket classifier instead of calling GPT-4; keeping customer text on-prem was a hard requirement from legal.
Decision: run local agent memory on SQLite in WAL mode; single-writer workloads plus zero configuration beat running a dedicated database server per project.
Preference: weekly research reports should be bullet-point summaries, maximum one page, with links to raw notebooks appended at the bottom.
Preference: use ruff for both linting and formatting in Python projects; it replaces flake8, isort, and black with one fast tool.
Preference: dashboards are dark-mode-first and every chart must remain readable under colorblind-safe palettes.
Preference: keep meetings under 25 minutes, send the agenda at least one day ahead, and cancel any meeting without an agenda.

SOP deployment: run the full test suite, then docker compose build, tag the release image, push it to the registry, deploy to staging first, verify the health endpoint returns ok, then promote the same image tag to production. Never hand-edit files on servers.

SOP new dataset intake: verify the checksum, lint the schema against the registered contract, register the dataset in the catalog, run a 50-row preview validation, then announce it in the data channel with the catalog link.

SOP credential rotation: generate the new secret in the vault, update .env.prod through the secrets manager only, restart affected services, confirm health checks pass, and log the rotation date in the audit sheet.

SOP incident response: page the on-call engineer immediately, open an incident doc from the template, post status updates every 30 minutes until resolved, and file a blameless postmortem within 72 hours.

SOP paper submission checklist: anonymize author info, attach the reproducibility appendix, verify every citation resolves, audit licenses of released assets, and get supervisor sign-off before upload.
As of March 2026 the vector store runs FAISS on the staging node for all similarity queries.
Since June 2026 the vector store migrated from FAISS to Qdrant so we can support filtered similarity search in production.
The team used Label Studio for all annotation work until April 2026.
In May 2026 annotation moved from Label Studio to Argilla because Argilla integrates natively with our FastAPI labeling service.
The weekly research sync used to be scheduled on Thursdays at 10:00 CET.
From July 2026 onward the weekly research sync takes place on Tuesdays at 14:00 CET.
As of January 2026 the GPU cluster consists of eight A100 cards.
After the August 2026 expansion the GPU cluster runs sixteen A100s plus four H100s.
Project Aurora is our retrieval-augmented generation evaluation harness; Priya Nair leads it and the goal is reproducible RAG benchmarks across changing corpora.
Project Borealis is the time-series forecasting benchmark built with Nordwind Energy using wind-farm telemetry data.
Dr. Elena Vasquez is principal investigator for model alignment research; she is based at the Madrid satellite office.
Tomas Lindqvist is the infrastructure engineer who maintains the GPU cluster, deploy pipelines, and backup schedules.
Helios Research Lab is a 40-person applied research lab in Utrecht focused on agentic systems and evaluation tooling.
PaperTrail is the internal literature tracker; it indexes arXiv daily, flags citations that appear in our drafts, and sends digest emails each morning.
Qdrant is the production vector database for filtered similarity search over experiment embeddings.
As of March 2026 all experiments log metrics and artifacts to the MLflow tracking server on staging-02.
Until February 2026 documentation was hosted on ReadTheDocs; since then we self-host MkDocs behind the internal gateway.
During Q1 2026 user studies were run in-house only; the external pilot program began in April 2026.
Starting March 2026 the budget review cycle changed from quarterly to monthly.
Decision: embedding vectors are cached in Redis with a 24-hour TTL, which cut recompute costs by roughly forty percent.
We cache computed embeddings inside Redis using a TTL of twenty-four hours; recompute cost dropped by approximately 40% after this change.
Each service caps its Postgres connection pool at 20 connections so the combined load never exceeds max_connections.
Postgres pools are limited to a maximum of twenty connections per service instance to avoid hitting the database max_connections ceiling.
Redis was evaluated for session storage but rejected; persistence requirements pointed us to Postgres-backed sessions instead.
MongoDB was considered for the metrics store but rejected due to weak join support and the operational cost of sharding.
Kafka stays on the technology watchlist in case event volume ever exceeds 50k messages per second.
FAISS still powers the offline batch similarity jobs over archived historical snapshots even though online search moved elsewhere.
Every experiment must seed its RNG with seed 42 by default and record an environment hash alongside results for reproducibility.
Weekly model evaluation procedure: pull the latest checkpoint, run the HELM subset suite, compare scores against the current champion, and record the delta on the evaluation dashboard.
The analytics data warehouse is BigQuery; raw event data lands hourly through scheduled transfer jobs.
Decision: adopt OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing across all services because vendor-neutral exporters simplified our observability stack and avoided lock-in.
Nordwind Energy is the external partner supplying wind-farm telemetry that powers the Borealis forecasting benchmark.
As of April 2026 Priya Nair serves as tech lead of Project Aurora, taking over after Marco's departure to a professorship.
The internal wiki runs on Outline; legacy Confluence exports were archived and remain available read-only.
Code reviews should complete within one business day; pull requests larger than 400 changed lines require a pairing session instead of async review.
SDK release procedure: update the changelog, run integration tests, publish a canary under the next dist-tag, soak for 48 hours monitoring error rates, then promote the canary version to latest.
Decision: use Bun's built-in test runner for unit tests instead of Vitest; the single-binary runtime keeps CI pipelines under two minutes.
H100 nodes are reserved for RLHF training runs while the A100 pool handles everything else, following Tomas Lindqvist's scheduling policy.
Staging database snapshots run nightly at 02:00 UTC with seven-day retention.
Nightly backups of the staging Postgres database happen at two in the morning UTC and are kept for one week.
Production backups follow a different schedule: monthly cold-storage archives with one-year retention, tested quarterly by restore drills.
Until June 2026 experiment configurations lived in YAML files inside each repo; they moved to the central config service Confidant in July 2026.
Project Aurora depends on PaperTrail for automated citation checks and on Qdrant for its retrieval index.
The lab office moved from Utrecht city center to the Utrecht Science Park campus in February 2026.
Decision: all new services standardize on Python 3.12; version 3.11 is allowed only when legacy dependencies lack compatible wheels.
